Pattern 2: Sticky Footer 📌
Sticky Footer HTML/CSS
slides.codeSnippet:
<body>
  <header>Header</header>
  <main>Content</main>
  <footer>Footer</footer>
</body>

body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 100vh; }
main { flex: 1; }

slides.title: Pattern 4: Card Grid with Equal Height 📇

quizData.question: In the sticky footer pattern, what does `main { flex: 1; }` do?

options.text: Makes the main content a flex container
Allows the main element to grow and fill the available vertical space, pushing the footer down

quizData.explanation: `flex: 1;` on `<main>` makes it take up remaining space, keeping the footer at the bottom.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Don't Over‑Flex

Not every container needs to be flex. Use flex when you need alignment or distribution of space; otherwise a simple block or inline layout may be enough.
